0.question: How far in advance should I book my Machu Picchu tour?
0.answer: We recommend booking at least 2 weeks in advance, especially during peak season (June–August). Group sizes are limited to ensure a personalized experience.

1.question: What's included in the tour price?
1.answer: Our tours include transportation from your hotel in Cusco, entrance to archaeological sites, a bilingual professional guide, and a buffet lunch. Some premium tours include the return train ride.

2.question: Is it safe to travel to Machu Picchu?
2.answer: Yes, it's completely safe. Cusco and Machu Picchu are well-organized tourist destinations. Our guides are certified in first aid and carry emergency kits. We also offer optional travel insurance.

3.question: What should I bring on the tour?
3.answer: Original passport (required), sunscreen, hat, water, comfortable layered clothing, trekking shoes, rain jacket (November–March), and a camera.

4.question: Can I cancel or reschedule my booking?
4.answer: Yes, we offer free cancellation up to 48 hours before the tour. For rescheduling, contact us at least 24 hours in advance and we'll adjust the date at no extra cost, subject to availability.

5.question: Are there age or fitness restrictions?
5.answer: Most of our tours are suitable for all ages. However, some trekking tours (Rainbow Mountain, Salkantay) require good physical fitness. We recommend acclimatizing for 2–3 days in Cusco before high-altitude tours.

6.question: What payment methods do you accept?
6.answer: We accept credit and debit cards (Visa, Mastercard, American Express) through Culqi, as well as PayPal for international payments. All payments are processed with SSL encryption.

0.title: 10 Essential Tips for Visiting Machu Picchu
0.excerpt: Everything you need to know before your first visit to the Inca citadel. From acclimatization to what to pack in your backpack.
0.author: Machu Picchu Travel
0.intro: Visiting the magical citadel of Machu Picchu is undoubtedly one of the most desired experiences for travelers worldwide. However, due to its geographic location and conservation regulations, planning this trip requires some preparation. To make your adventure seamless and perfect, we have prepared a list of the 10 most essential tips you should keep in mind.

sections.title: 1. Book your tickets well in advance
paragraphs: Machu Picchu entrance tickets have a strict daily limit established by the Peruvian government to protect the archaeological heritage. During high season (May to October), tickets can sell out 3 to 4 months in advance. We advise you to book as soon as you decide on your travel dates using a trusted service like our [Machu Picchu Full Day](/tours/machu-picchu-full-day), choosing the circuit that best fits your physical expectations and exploration goals.

sections.title: 2. Understand the new visiting circuits
paragraphs: Machu Picchu is no longer explored freely. Currently, there are three one-way circuits: Circuit 1 (panoramic and high terraces), Circuit 2 (classic and complete, the most recommended), and Circuit 3 (lower part and royal areas). Make sure to choose the correct ticket, as once inside you cannot change routes or go back on your steps.

sections.title: 3. Plan for altitude acclimatization
paragraphs: The city of Cusco is located at about 3,400 meters (11,150 feet) above sea level, while Machu Picchu is at about 2,430 meters (7,970 feet). Altitude sickness or 'soroche' is very common upon arrival. The ideal is to spend at least 1 or 2 days in Cusco or the Sacred Valley (which is at a lower altitude) before doing demanding hikes like the famous [Rainbow Mountain (Vinicunca)](/tours/montana-de-colores-vinicunca). Drink plenty of water, sip hot coca tea, and avoid heavy meals for the first few days.

sections.title: 4. Hire an official tour guide
paragraphs: Exploring Machu Picchu without a guide is missing half the magic. Official guides will reveal the history of the temples, the sophisticated agricultural terrace system, the astronomical alignments, and the theories behind its abandonment. You can hire a certified guide in advance through our agency or at the gates of the sanctuary.

sections.title: 5. Choose the ideal mode of transportation
paragraphs: To reach Aguas Calientes (Machu Picchu Town), the fastest and most comfortable way is by train from Ollantaytambo or Poroy. If you are looking for a unique and adventurous experience, the classic 4-day Inca Trail or the short 2-day route are excellent choices. Plan your rail connections and bus transfers carefully to avoid missing your entry times.

sections.title: 6. Dress in layers and prepare for the weather
paragraphs: Machu Picchu is located in a cloud forest zone, meaning the weather is highly changeable. Early in the morning it can be very cold and misty, but by midday the sun can be intense. We recommend dressing in layers: a breathable t-shirt, a light fleece, a windbreaker or rain jacket, and comfortable trousers.

sections.title: 7. Bring insect repellent and sunscreen
paragraphs: Surrounded by humid subtropical forest, Machu Picchu is home to very small mosquitoes whose bites cause intense itching. Always bring a good insect repellent and apply it regularly. Similarly, the high-altitude sun can burn your skin quickly, so wear a hat and high-factor sunscreen.

sections.title: 8. Know the luggage restrictions and prohibited items
paragraphs: Machu Picchu regulations prohibit entry with backpacks exceeding 40x35x20 cm, large umbrellas (rain ponchos are allowed), tripods or camera stabilizers, drones, and single-use plastic containers. There is a locker service at the entrance where you can leave your belongings for an extra fee.

sections.title: 9. Carry cash in Soles
paragraphs: Although many shops in Aguas Calientes accept credit cards, it is essential to carry cash in Peruvian Soles (PEN). You will need it to pay for the public restrooms located only outside the sanctuary, buy reusable water bottles, snacks, or tip your guides.

sections.title: 10. Get the official Machu Picchu stamp in your passport
paragraphs: As a special keepsake of your visit, don't forget to stamp your passport with the commemorative Machu Picchu stamp. There is a small office with a self-service wooden stamp right next to the exit of the archaeological park. It is free and represents a beautiful souvenir of your journey to Peru.

0.conclusion: Visiting Machu Picchu is a life-changing experience. Planning every detail ahead of time will not only save you stress but also allow you to fully immerse yourself in the majesty of this sacred place. If you want us to organize your complete trip from start to finish, don't hesitate to contact our travel advisors.

1.title: Sacred Valley: The Hidden Gem of the Andes
1.excerpt: Discover why the Sacred Valley of the Incas is much more than just a gateway to Machu Picchu.
1.author: Machu Picchu Travel
1.intro: The Sacred Valley of the Incas is one of the most beautiful and historic destinations in the Cusco region. Stretching along the Vilcanota River, this fertile valley boasts an exceptional mild climate and houses breathtaking archaeological complexes that rival the beauty of Machu Picchu itself. In this guide, we discover the main attractions that make the Sacred Valley an essential stop on your trip.

sections.title: Pisac: Imperial ruins and traditional market
paragraphs: Located about 30 kilometers from Cusco, Pisac is famous for its stunning archaeological complex perched high on a mountain. Walking through its agricultural terraces, ceremonial temples, and ancient Inca cemetery is an amazing experience. In the lower town, the Pisac artisan market comes alive with colorful textiles, handmade ceramics, and beautiful silver jewelry.

sections.title: Ollantaytambo: The last living Inca town
paragraphs: Ollantaytambo is one of the few places in Peru where residents still live in original Inca constructions. Its cobbled streets, running water channels, and traditional houses will transport you back in time. The imposing military fortress crowning the town was the site of one of the few battles where the Incas defeated the Spanish conquistadors, offering spectacular views of the valley.

sections.title: Maras and Moray: Millenary salt pans and agricultural laboratories
paragraphs: The salt pans of Maras are a stunning visual spectacle: over 3,000 pink salt pools fed by a warm underground spring that have been harvested since pre-Inca times. Nearby lies Moray, a set of impressive concentric agricultural terraces resembling an amphitheater. Moray worked as an Inca agricultural research laboratory, where they experimented with different crops under specific microclimates.

sections.title: Chinchero: The town of the rainbow and cradle of Andean weaving
paragraphs: Situated at a high altitude, Chinchero retains a very pure Andean charm. It houses a beautiful colonial church built over an Inca palace and extensive agricultural terraces. However, its main attraction lies in its traditional weaving centers, where local women dressed in typical attire demonstrate the washing, spinning, and dyeing of alpaca wool using only local plants, flowers, and minerals.

1.conclusion: The Sacred Valley offers a fascinating journey through the history, living culture, and natural landscapes of the Andes. We recommend spending at least two full days exploring its wonders before continuing to Machu Picchu. Check out our daily [Sacred Valley VIP](/tours/valle-sagrado-vip) tour or the [Sacred Valley Traditional](/tours/valle-sagrado-tradicional) tour to plan your perfect itinerary.

2.title: Complete Guide: Rainbow Mountain (Vinicunca)
2.excerpt: Altitude, difficulty, best season, and everything you need for this one-of-a-kind hike.
2.author: Machu Picchu Travel
2.intro: The Mountain of Seven Colors, also known as Vinicunca, has become the second most visited tourist attraction in Cusco after Machu Picchu. This extraordinary natural landscape, situated at a high altitude, resembles an oil painting with its stripes of reddish, golden, green, and purple hues. To enjoy this demanding but wonderful hike, we present our complete preparation guide.

sections.title: Where do the colors of Vinicunca come from?
paragraphs: The surprising coloration of the mountain is due to a complex geological history and the accumulation of different mineral layers deposited over millions of years. The red hue comes from clay rich in iron; pink stripes are caused by red clay and mud; green is the result of phyllites and clays rich in magnesium and iron; golden hues are due to calcareous sandstones rich in sulfur; and purple comes from limonite.

sections.title: The Altitude: The real challenge of the trail
paragraphs: The hike to Vinicunca is not technically difficult or steep, but the altitude is the real challenge. The route begins at about 4,600 meters (15,090 feet) high, and the main viewpoint is located at the astonishing altitude of 5,036 meters (16,520 feet) above sea level. At this elevation, the air is thinner and oxygen is scarce. Therefore, it is absolutely mandatory to have spent at least 2 or 3 days acclimatizing in Cusco or the Sacred Valley before attempting this hike.

sections.title: Tips for a successful hike
paragraphs: To fully enjoy the hike, we advise you to walk at your own steady, unhurried pace and breathe deeply. Using trekking poles is highly useful for balance and reducing knee strain. Bring coca leaves to chew or pills for soroche. Additionally, you can rent a horse from local residents at the start of the trail if you feel the physical effort is too much.

sections.title: What to pack in your daypack
paragraphs: The weather in the high mountains is extremely cold and windy, but the hike will raise your body temperature. Dress in light thermal layers and bring a high-quality windbreaker jacket. Don't forget a wool hat, gloves, high-factor sunscreen (radiation is very high at altitude), sunglasses, and enough water to stay hydrated. Also bring cash to pay for the restrooms along the route.

2.conclusion: Reaching the Vinicunca viewpoint and contemplating the rainbow earth in front of the imposing Mount Ausangate is an experience you will remember for the rest of your life. With proper preparation and responsible acclimatization, you will conquer this Andean peak safely. Join our daily tour to [Rainbow Mountain](/tours/montana-de-colores-vinicunca) with certified guides and transportation included.

3.title: Cusco Cuisine: Flavors You Can't Miss
3.excerpt: A journey through Cusco's traditional dishes that every traveler should try during their stay.
3.author: Machu Picchu Travel
3.intro: Cusco is not only the archaeological capital of America but also an exceptional gastronomic destination that delights the most demanding palates. Cusco cuisine stands out for fusing millenary Andean ingredients (such as quinoa, native potatoes, giant corn, and aromatic herbs) with contemporary Spanish and Creole cooking techniques. In this guide, we invite you to discover the traditional dishes and ingredients you must try during your visit.

sections.title: Pachamanca: The sacred feast under the earth
paragraphs: Pachamanca is not just a plate of food; it is an ancient Andean ritual of gratitude to Mother Earth (Pachamama). It consists of cooking different types of meat (chicken, pork, lamb, alpaca) and tubers (potatoes, sweet potatoes, broad beans) using preheated stones placed in an oven dug into the ground. Everything is covered with banana leaves, local aromatic herbs like huacatay, and soil, achieving a slow cook with unmatched smoky flavors.

sections.title: Alpaca Lomo Saltado: A Peruvian classic with an Andean twist
paragraphs: Alpaca lomo saltado is the flagship dish of Chinese-Peruvian fusion cuisine. In Cusco, local and gourmet restaurants often prepare this delicacy by substituting beef with alpaca meat, a highly tender, lean, healthy, and low-cholesterol option. Sautéed in a wok over high heat with onions, tomatoes, yellow pepper, and fresh cilantro, it is served with crispy native French fries and hot white rice.

sections.title: Cuy Chactado and Roasted: Ancient Andean tradition
paragraphs: The cuy (guinea pig) has been one of the most important sources of protein in the Andean diet since the Inca era. In traditional Cusco picanterías, it is served roasted, seasoned with herbs like huacatay and accompanied by stuffed rocoto pepper and potatoes, or deep-fried under a heavy stone (Cuy Chactado), which gives it a very crispy texture. It is a dish full of tradition and local flavor.

sections.title: Chairo and Cusco soups for the cold
paragraphs: For cold Andean nights, there is nothing better than a hot Cusco soup. Chairo is a hearty, thick soup made of chuño (dehydrated potato), mutton, beef, wheat, corn hominy, and vegetables. Another delicious specialty is Quinoa Soup, nutritious and comforting. Always accompany them with a hot cup of coca or muña tea, herbs that significantly aid digestion at high altitude.

3.conclusion: Exploring Cusco through its flavors is a wonderful cultural experience. From rustic traditional picanterías to the most award-winning gourmet restaurants, Cusco has a culinary proposal that will surprise you. If you want to experience the preparation of traditional Andean Pachamanca up close, book our [Pachamanca Tour in Chinchero](/tours/pachamanca-full-day) today.
